sn22.96:1.2: “That” (_so_) refers back to an introductory passage that has been elided.
sn22.96:3.1: These details are greatly expanded in [dn17](), where the Buddha names himself Mahāsudassana.
sn22.96:3.5: “Silver“ is omitted by mistake in MS edition.
sn22.96:3.6: _Hema_ (“snow gold”) evokes the golden radiance of a snowy mountain in the dawn light, a blessing of the gods that, it may easily be imagined, leaves its traces in the gold found in abundance in its streams.
sn22.96:3.12: _Dukūla_ is a delicate cloth produced from the inner bark of a tree. | _Sandāna_ is a tether or “halter” for cows or horses (Rig Veda 1.162.8) or even for binding foes (Atharva Veda 6.103).
sn22.96:4.8: Read _vessinī_ per [dn17:2.15.8](). the  “peasant” there are several variants, mostly obscure. One is _velāmikā_, explained by the commentary as of mixed brahmin and aristocrat parentage, which agrees with Sanskrit _vilomaja_, but this could be a rationalization under later influence. At [an9.20]() we have a brahmin named Velāma, a past life of the Buddha who gave a magnificent offering consisting of the same things mentioned in this Sutta. This is surely more than a coincidence, but it is hard to explain.
